answer: Each agent may keep only one live work thread, locked to a slowly vesting ferrous bond that slashes if the operator is later shown to run a cluster. Peers countersign outputs into an opal fingerprint of that thread; reused work, split bonds, or near-duplicate fingerprints are rejected. Forging many identities therefore means funding a distinct lockup and a distinct, independently attested history for every clone, which costs far more than creating keys.
